methotrexate.t: 7.5 Methotrexate Concomitant use of hydroxychloroquine sulfate tablets and methotrexate may increase the incidence of adverse reactions.

digoxin.t: 7.7 Digoxin Concomitant hydroxychloroquine sulfate tablets and digoxin therapy may result in increased serum digoxin levels.
Monitor serum digoxin levels closely in patients receiving combined therapy.

chloroquine.t: 7.8 Cimetidine Concomitant use of cimetidine resulted in a 2-fold increase of exposure of chloroquine, which is structurally related to hydroxychloroquine.
7.10 Praziquantel Chloroquine has been reported to reduce the bioavailability of praziquantel.

rifampin.t: 7.9 Rifampicin Lack of efficacy of hydroxychloroquine was reported when rifampicin was concomitantly administered.

ampicillin.t: 7.12 Ampicillin In a study of healthy volunteers, chloroquine significantly reduced the bioavailability of ampicillin.
Interaction of ampicillin with hydroxychloroquine cannot be ruled out.

tamoxifen.t: Risk factors for retinal damage include daily hydroxychloroquine sulfate dosages ≥5 mg/kg of actual body weight, durations of use greater than five years, renal impairment, use of concomitant drug products such as tamoxifen citrate, and concurrent macular disease.

glucose.t: Measure blood glucose in patients presenting with clinical symptoms suggestive of hypoglycemia and as adjust the antidiabetic treatment as necessary.
5.6 Hemolytic Anemia Associated with G6PD Deficiency Hemolysis has been reported in patients with glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency.

qt.t: Therefore, hydroxychloroquine sulfate tablets are not recommended in patients taking other drugs that have the potential to prolong the QT interval or are arrhythmogenic [see Warnings and Precautions ( 5.1 )] .

anticonv.t: 7.4 Antiepileptics The activity of antiepileptic drugs might be impaired if co-administered with hydroxychloroquine sulfate tablets.

antacid.t: 7.11 Antacids and kaolin Antacids and kaolin can reduce absorption of chloroquine; an interval of at least 4 hours between intake of these agents and chloroquine should be observed.
Interaction of antacids and kaolin with hydroxychloroquine cannot be ruled out.

cortico.t: Corticosteroids, salicylates, and other antirheumatic agents may be used concomitantly with hydroxychloroquine sulfate tablets.
